title: Read a working's infinity and no-limit words as the judge does
body:
## Summary
rules/chain.ts kept its own INF and DNE patterns beside calc-read's infinityOf and DNE, and they drifted: a working line ending in the typographic minus infinity, 'undefined' or 'no limit' was left bare while the same text as the answer is judged.

## Description
The judge reads an infinity through desk/src/lib/rules/calc-read.ts:96 (infinityOf: '-', U+2212, inf, infinity, the infinity sign) and a no-limit word through desk/src/lib/rules/calc-read.ts:100 (dne, does not exist, no limit, undefined). The chain checker had desk/src/lib/rules/chain.ts:136-137 (old) with a hyphen-only sign and only dne / does not exist, used by limitLine and by the tagger's sameAt (chain.ts:397 old). Registry law one-authority-per-vocabulary (judgment-guardbands): two hand copies of one vocabulary drift. Fixed: both sites read through infinityOf and DNE.

## Flow
- learner writes 'lim_(x->0) -1/x^2 = −∞' (phone keyboard minus) -> chainChecks -> limitLine -> INF no match -> constantValue null -> null: the correct line is never ticked
- 'lim_(x->0) sin(x)/x = undefined' -> null, never rung, though checkAnswer marks 'undefined' wrong
- fix: limitLine and sameAt call infinityOf / DNE

## Expected impact
A learner's correct infinite-limit line is ticked and a wrong no-limit line is rung, as the answer is. Could break: nothing found; 21 suites green.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a working line reads an infinity and a no-limit word as the answer does
Before: 2/13 probe lines read as the judge reads them (tools/chain-rules-test.cjs new test, red)
After: 13/13 (green), re-measured on the commit
Method: gate - new test in tools/chain-rules-test.cjs, red before, green after
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A sequence limit's leak check reads algebra said in words, as Calculus 1's does
body:
## Summary
calc2.ts sequenceLeaks says it copies calc.ts leaksCalc's limit rule but read the line without algebraSaid and without the long pass, so 'The limit is e squared.' leaked on a Calculus 1 limit and not on the same sequence.

## Description
desk/src/lib/rules/calc.ts leaksCalcOnce reads `algebraSaid(spoken(line))` and runs a 7..24-token long pass; desk/src/lib/rules/calc2.ts sequenceLeaks (doc: 'Calculus 1's rule for a limit (calc.ts leaksCalc, copied)') read `spoken(line)` only and windows of up to 6 tokens. The parity test in tools/calc2-sequence-test.cjs used a hand list with no 'squared/plus/minus/times' line, so it could not see the gap (§4.7). Fixed: algebraSaid moved to calc-read.ts (one definition) and sequenceLeaks reads through it with calc.ts's long pass. Withholding is the product.

## Flow
- hint on lim a_n, a_n=(1+2/n)^n says 'The limit is e squared.' -> sequenceLeaks -> no window reads e^2 -> hint shown with the answer
- same line on the Calculus 1 limit at infinity -> algebraSaid -> 'e^2' -> refused
- fix: algebraSaid in calc-read, imported by both; long pass added

## Expected impact
A Calculus 2 learner can no longer be told a sequence's limit in words the Calculus 1 check already catches. Could break: more hint lines refused on sequence items (only adds hits).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the sequence leak check refuses every line the Calculus 1 limit check refuses
Before: 18/108 (limit, line) pairs disagree (9 limits x 12 lines)
After: 0/108, re-measured on the commit; parity test extended by 9 lines, red then green
Method: gate - tools/calc2-sequence-test.cjs leak parity, plus a 108-pair probe
Result: better
Gate: none

title: One answer-key list for every Calculus spec; Calculus 1 refuses 'result' too
body:
## Summary
The rule 'a spec carries no answer field' was a literal list typed seven times; calc.ts's five copies lacked 'result', calc2.ts's two had it, so a Calculus 1 or implicit spec with result: '2x' was well formed and printed.

## Description
desk/src/lib/rules/calc.ts:192, :326, :1237, :1246, :1283 (old) each `["answer", "truth", "solution", "value"]`; desk/src/lib/rules/calc2.ts:148, :460 `["answer", "solution", "truth", "value", "result"]`. The header of calc.ts states 'The spec carries NO answer field'. Registry law one-authority-per-vocabulary. Fixed: ANSWER_KEYS and carriesAnswer() in desk/src/lib/rules/calc-read.ts, called at all seven sites.

## Flow
- a spec {shape:'derivative', f:'x^2', result:'2x'} reaches wellFormed -> read() checks four keys -> ok:true
- the same key on approx-integral -> refused
- fix: one list, one helper

## Expected impact
Every Calculus shape refuses the same answer-bearing keys; the next key added is added once. Could break: a stored spec carrying 'result' now reads as malformed (none found in fixtures).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every shape refuses every answer key
Before: 26/30 (6 shapes x 5 keys) refused; 7 literal copies
After: 30/30 refused; 1 list, re-measured on the commit
Method: gate - new test in tools/calc-rules-test.cjs, red before, green after
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
grep '"answer", "truth", "solution", "value"' desk/src/lib/rules/calc.ts -> 5 lines (192, 326, 1237, 1246, 1283)
grep '"result"' desk/src/lib/rules/calc2.ts -> 148, 460
probe: wellFormed({shape:'derivative',f:'x^2',result:'2x'}).ok -> true

title: Hold the spine's shape contract to rules/calc CALC_SHAPES, not only to its own copy
body:
## Summary
calculus1.spine.ts calls its ten shape ids a contract with rules/calc.ts, 'listed again in tools/maths-paths-test.cjs', but the test only checked the spine against that copy: a shape added to CALC_SHAPES passed.

## Description
desk/src/lib/library/calculus1.spine.ts:13-16 names the contract; tools/maths-paths-test.cjs:22 holds a hand SHAPES list and test 4 compares the spine with it, never with desk/src/lib/rules/calc.ts:50 CALC_SHAPES (§4.7: a test that reads its own list). Fixed: test 4 reads CALC_SHAPES from calc.ts's comment-stripped source (a require would put rules/ in the module cache test 12 holds clean) and asserts the same set.

## Flow
- seed an 11th id 'related-rate' into CALC_SHAPES
- run tools/maths-paths-test.cjs -> exit 0 before (drift passes)
- after the change -> exit 1 (drift caught); clean tree exit 0

## Expected impact
A shape added or renamed in the engine without the spine (or the reverse) is caught by the rules gate. Could break: nothing; test-only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the contract is checked on both sides
Before: seeded drift: maths-paths-test exit 0
After: seeded drift: exit 1; clean exit 0, re-measured on the commit
Method: gate - seeded violation, then reverted
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten

title: The Calculus leak check reads a hint written in Czech notation (tg, cotg, arctg)
body:
## Summary
A cz learner's hint prompt is told the school writes tg and cotg, and the judge reads tg in a cz answer, but leaksCalc read hints with the engine's names only: 'Výsledek je tg x + C.' gave away int 1/cos(x)^2 dx unrefused.

## Description
desk/src/lib/desk/read.ts:28 notationLine tells a cz hint 'tg and cotg for tan and cot'; desk/src/lib/rules/calc.ts checkAnswer reads a cz answer through czechAnswer (calc-read czechNames), so 'tg x + C' is right; desk/src/lib/rules/calc.ts leaksCalc and desk/src/lib/rules/calc2.ts withPointed never applied czechNames, and desk/src/lib/desk/hint.ts:120 passes no system to leaksCalc. Fixed: both leak checks also read the line through czechNames, for every learner (like the MK4 comma pass). Withholding is the product.

## Flow
- cz learner asks for a hint on 'Find int 1/cos(x)^2 dx' -> model, primed with tg notation, writes 'Výsledek je tg x + C.'
- leaksCalc -> compile('tg x') null -> no leak -> the answer is on the TV
- fix: czechNames pass -> 'tan x + C' -> refused

## Expected impact
A Czech learner's hint can no longer state the answer in school notation. Could break: a Czech hint naming tg x where tan x IS the answer is now refused (intended).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - Czech-notation lines that state the answer are refused
Before: 0/4 probe lines refused (tools/calc-rules-test.cjs new test, red)
After: 4/4 refused, 4 control lines unchanged, re-measured on the commit
Method: gate - new test, red before, green after; 20 suites green
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
probe before: leaksCalc({shape:'antiderivative',f:'1/cos(x)^2'},'Výsledek je tg x + C.') -> false; checkAnswer(same spec,'tg x + C','cz') -> right
desk/src/lib/desk/read.ts:28 '... tg and cotg for tan and cot ...'
desk/src/lib/desk/hint.ts:120 leaksCalc(spec.calc, line) - no system

title: Three module headers that misstate what the module imports or holds
body:
## Summary
calc.ts, chain.ts and calc-word.ts headers stated import lists or a shape count the code contradicts.

## Description
desk/src/lib/rules/calc.ts:15 said it imports only calc-expr, calc-read and calc2 (it also imports taskText, which tools/calc2-seam-test.cjs test 2 pins); desk/src/lib/rules/chain.ts:2-3 said it is built only on calc-expr and calc's tolerances (it imports calc-read, calc2, taskText); desk/src/lib/rules/calc-word.ts:5 said 'one of the nine shapes' (CALC_SHAPES has ten). Comments fixed.

## Flow
- read each header against its import lines and CALC_SHAPES
- fix the three sentences

## Expected impact
A reader (or a builder model) trusting the header gets the true dependency list. Could break: nothing; comments only.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - headers match the code
Before: 3 header claims contradicted by import lines / CALC_SHAPES
After: 0
Method: gate - tsc, seam, chain and word suites green on the commit
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/rules/calc.ts:18 import ... from "./taskText" vs :15 'imports only calc-expr.ts, calc-read.ts and calc2.ts'
desk/src/lib/rules/calc-word.ts:5 'one of the nine shapes'

title: A decimal in brackets is the same decimal on every limit and integral
body:
## Summary
calc2's ruling 28 reads '(0.6956)' as the decimal it wraps, but calc.ts judgeNumber and calc2's sequence judgeLimit asked isDecimal of the raw answer: '(0.38)' on a limit of 3/8 was marked wrong while '0.38' was right.

## Description
desk/src/lib/rules/calc2.ts readsAsDecimal (ruling 28) unwraps brackets and a sign; desk/src/lib/rules/calc.ts judgeNumber and calc2.ts judgeLimit used `isDecimal(written)` (desk/src/lib/rules/calc-read.ts:102), so a bracketed rounding fell to the exact path and was 'wrong' - a false ring (MB-B28 calls a false tick a blocker). Fixed: decimalNumeral in calc-read (spaces, enclosing ( ) [ ] { } and one sign set aside), called by all three; decimalCall reads places off the bare numeral.

## Flow
- learner answers '(0.38)' to lim 3x/(8x+1) at infinity -> isDecimal false -> exact 1e-6 -> wrong
- '0.38' -> decimalCall -> correct rounding -> right
- fix: decimalNumeral -> '0.38' -> right

## Expected impact
A learner who brackets a rounded value gets the verdict the bare value gets. Could break: such answers on evaluate-type shapes now read 'unsure' (rounded) instead of 'wrong'.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - bracketed and bare decimals get one verdict
Before: 9/18 bracketed forms agree with their bare form
After: 18/18, re-measured on the commit
Method: gate - new test in tools/calc-rules-test.cjs, red before, green after; frozen table unchanged
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
probe before: checkAnswer({shape:'limit',f:'3x/(8x+1)',at:'inf'},'(0.38)') -> wrong; '0.38' -> right; checkAnswer({shape:'definite-integral',f:'x^2',a:0,b:1},'(0.33)') -> wrong
desk/src/lib/rules/calc.ts judgeNumber (before): const decimal = isDecimal(written);

title: A limit at infinity whose limit is infinite leaks in its own question, so it is never set
body:
## Summary
leaksCalc and sequenceLeaks treat any mention of infinity as a leak when the truth is infinite, before setting the question's own notation aside, so 'Find lim_(x->infinity) x^2/(x+1).' leaks itself and items.ts drops every such spec - while the sequence-limit set line asks the model for terms that 'grow without bound'.

## Description
desk/src/lib/rules/calc.ts:672 leaksCalcOnce: `if (truth.kind === "inf") return /infinit|∞|\binf\b/.test(text);` runs before ownPieces are removed; desk/src/lib/rules/calc2.ts:559 sequenceLeaks the same. desk/src/lib/desk/items.ts:422 drops a spec whose printed question leaks. desk/src/lib/desk/items.ts:279 (sequence-limit line) and docs/concepts/STUDY-DESK-V2-PLAN.md:666 (ruling 40) ask for terms that 'grow without bound'; docs/MATH-COURSE-PATHS.md:454 rules 'on an infinite limit, the line names infinity at all'. The two rulings conflict: either the infinite case is not a question the desk sets (refuse it in wellFormed, fix the set line), or the leak check sets the question's own 'x -> infinity' aside first (a loosening of a withholding rule). Every hint on such an item a reading page brings in is also withheld (it must say 'as x approaches infinity').

## Flow
- model returns {shape:'sequence-limit', f:'2^x/x^3'} as the set line asks
- wellFormed ok -> question 'Find lim_(n->infinity) a_n, where a_n = 2^n/n^3.' -> leaksCalc(spec, question) true -> dropped
- a page item 'Find lim_(x->infinity) e^x' read by specFromQuestion -> every hint that says 'as x approaches infinity' is refused -> the fixed withheld line

## Expected impact
Owner decides whether divergent limits are asked. Today: 6/9 probed infinite-limit specs are unaskable and their tokens are spent. Could break: under the loosening option, a line that says 'x approaches infinity and so does f' still leaks; a terser 'both go to infinity' would too.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an infinite limit at infinity is either askable or not asked for
Before: 6/6 well-formed infinite limits at +-infinity (3 sequences, 3 limits) leak in their own printed question; 0/3 finite ones do
After: unmeasurable until the direction is chosen: option A (refuse in wellFormed) gives 0 asked and 0 wasted; option B (pieces first) gives 0/6 self-leaks
Method: probe - question() and leaksCalc on 9 specs; the rung above needs the ruling
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-loosen
evidence:
probe: leaksCalc({shape:'limit',f:'x^2/(x+1)',at:'inf'}, 'Find lim_(x->infinity) x^2/(x+1).') -> true
leaksCalc({shape:'sequence-limit',f:'2^x/x^3'}, 'Find lim_(n->infinity) a_n, where a_n = 2^n/n^3.') -> true
desk/src/lib/desk/items.ts:422 if (!q || leaksCalc(c.spec, q.plain)) continue;
desk/src/lib/desk/items.ts:279 '... has a limit or grows without bound.'

title: English arccot, arcsec, arccsc are unreadable while Czech arccotg reads
body:
## Summary
The expression engine has no arccot/acot/arcsec/arccsc, so an English learner's 'arccot(x) + C' is 'cannot read', while a Czech learner's 'arccotg(x) + C' is judged right through czechNames.

## Description
desk/src/lib/rules/calc-expr.ts:103-113 WORDS has arcsin/arccos/arctan only; desk/src/lib/rules/calc-read.ts czechNames maps arccotg to (pi/2 - arctan(u)). Stewart (the course text) uses cot^-1 and arccot. Fix shape: add arccot/acot as a reading (FnName, FNS, TEX_FN, chain.ts OUTER - Record<FnName> forces all four), or expand 'arccot u' the way czechNames does for every learner. M across calc-expr and chain.

## Flow
- uk learner answers int -1/(1+x^2) dx with 'arccot(x) + C' -> compile null -> unsure 'cannot read'
- cz learner writes 'arccotg(x) + C' -> right
- specFromQuestion('Differentiate f(x) = arccot(x)') -> null; the cz form reads

## Expected impact
English Calculus learners can use the inverse cotangent the textbook teaches. Could break: the lexer's longest-first split ('arccos' vs 'arccot') and the frozen table.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the inverse cot reads in English as it does in Czech
Before: compile('arccot(x)') null; 4/4 English forms unreadable; checkAnswer English 'unsure', Czech 'right'
After: expected 4/4 readable, verdicts equal across systems (not built)
Method: simulation - three walked answers and one page text; the build crosses two files and the lexer
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
probe: compile('arccot(x)') null, compile('acot(x)') null, compile('arcsec(x)') null
checkAnswer({shape:'antiderivative',f:'-1/(1+x^2)'},'arccot(x) + C') -> unsure; with 'arccotg(x) + C','cz' -> right
instrument: a rules test over 'arccot(x)', 'acot x', 'arcsec(x)', 'arccsc(x)' as answers and specs: compile reads each, checkAnswer on d/dx arccot(x) = -1/(1+x^2) is right, chain-rules OUTER derives each; the frozen Calculus 1 table must stay byte for byte (calc2-seam-test 1)

title: An answer in n on a sequence item is called 'cannot read as mathematics'
body:
## Summary
A sequence's letter is n, but the judge reads x only: '1/n' gets 'The desk cannot read this answer as mathematics', while 'x' gets 'The answer should be a number, and this one depends on x.' The implicit item has the same misdirect for y.

## Description
desk/src/lib/rules/calc2.ts sequenceCheck compiles the answer as written; an n fails the lexer (calc-expr.ts:141) -> WHY.unreadable. The learner wrote readable mathematics in the question's own letter; the right line is 'should be a number'. tools/calc2-sequence-test.cjs:82 pins 'n' in the parity list with Calculus 1 (whose letter is x), so the change crosses a ruling: the parity row must exclude n answers. desk/src/lib/rules/calc.ts implicitCheck returns WHY.notNumber ('depends on x') for an answer in y only.

## Flow
- sequence item 'Find lim_(n->infinity) a_n, where a_n = n/(n + 1).' -> learner types 'n/(n+1)'
- sequenceCheck -> compile null -> 'cannot read this answer as mathematics'
- fix: try the answer with n read as x (termOf's rename); if it reads in x -> 'should be a number, and this one depends on n'

## Expected impact
The learner is told what is actually wrong (a term, not a limit). Could break: the parity row with Calculus 1 for 'n'.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the not-a-number line names the letter the learner used
Before: 3/3 n-answers ('1/n', 'n/(n+1)', '2n') get 'cannot read'
After: expected 3/3 get 'depends on n' (not built: pinned parity row)
Method: probe - checkAnswer on 4 answers; build blocked by the pinned parity contract
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract
evidence:
probe: checkAnswer({shape:'sequence-limit',f:'x/(x+1)'},'1/n') -> unsure 'The desk cannot read this answer as mathematics, and it does not guess.'; 'x' -> 'The answer should be a number, and this one depends on x.'
tools/calc2-sequence-test.cjs:82 ANSWERS includes 'n'
instrument: a calc2-sequence-test row: '1/n', 'n/(n+1)', '2n' get the not-a-number line naming n; the parity row (ANSWERS includes 'n') is narrowed to answers with no n, with the ruling named

title: calc2.ts retypes about a dozen calc.ts helpers and 22 desk sentences
body:
## Summary
calc2.ts cannot import calc.ts (a cycle), so it re-declares num, tidy, numPlain, script, closeAt, wrapped, CLOSING, boundOf, paramOf, fnOf, single and the window scan, plus 9 WHY and 13 REJECT sentences; three of today's four parity defects (algebraSaid, the answer keys, the decimal numeral) were this duplication drifting.

## Description
desk/src/lib/rules/calc2.ts:17-18 says 'A few lines of calc.ts are written again here (num, BAD_SPEC)'; the actual copies: num (desk/src/lib/rules/calc2.ts:114 / desk/src/lib/rules/calc.ts:160), tidy, isSum, numPlain, script (desk/src/lib/rules/calc2.ts:187-191 / desk/src/lib/rules/calc.ts:310-314), closeAt + CLOSING + wrapped (desk/src/lib/rules/calc2.ts:215-227 / desk/src/lib/rules/calc.ts:828-841, calc2's boundOf handles '(' only where calc.ts handles ( [ {), paramOf, fnOf, boundOf, single (x3 incl. sequenceLeaks), WHY (9 sentences, desk/src/lib/rules/calc2.ts:73-83) and REJECT (13, desk/src/lib/rules/calc2.ts:86-102). calc-read.ts exists precisely as the shared leaf (its header: 'so a Calculus 2 shape reads an answer and a hint line exactly as Calculus 1 does'). Registry law one-authority-per-vocabulary.

## Flow
- move each helper to calc-read.ts unchanged, import back into both
- seam test 1 proves Calculus 1 words did not move
- count the duplicated helper lines before and after

## Expected impact
The next Calculus 2 shape (plan rows 41-46) is written against one reader, not a third copy. Could break: a subtle difference (boundOf's bracket set) chosen one way changes a calc2 reading.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one reader for both courses
Before: 12 helpers + 22 sentences declared twice; 3 parity defects fixed today came from such copies
After: not built (M, two modules plus the seam contract)
Method: simulation - the three drifts of this round walked as the evidence
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/rules/calc2.ts:18 'A few lines of calc.ts are written again here for that reason (num, BAD_SPEC)'
desk/src/lib/rules/calc2.ts:72 '// The same sentences calc.ts says (WHY, REJECT), written again'
desk/src/lib/rules/calc2.ts boundOf: if (s[0] === "(") vs desk/src/lib/rules/calc.ts boundOf: if (CLOSING[s[0]])
instrument: move the shared readers (num, tidy, numPlain, script, closeAt, wrapped, boundOf, paramOf, fnOf, single, the window scan) and the shared WHY/REJECT sentences into calc-read.ts; the gate is calc2-seam-test 1 (frozen Calculus 1 table byte for byte) + calc2-sequence-test parity + the line count of duplicated helpers before and after
